world_vs_purpose_boundary.world_true: Propositions whose meaning and truth conditions do not depend on which analytical purpose is active: source observations, permit text, structured limit and DMR records, mechanical joins, dates, and grounded semantic judgments accepted in C3.
world_vs_purpose_boundary.purpose_only: Decision outputs, applicability resolutions under purpose-specific policies, compliance/exceedance verdicts, obligation verdicts, missing-evidence classifications, and any threshold or interpretation that exists only to answer A/B/C.

A.objective: For Federal FY2025, determine which enforceable numeric discharge limit applies to each relevant facility, discharge point, parameter, and monitoring period for which reported measurements exist; determine whether each available reported measurement exceeds the applicable limit; distinguish enforceable numeric limits from report-only monitoring or monitoring with no numeric compliance comparison; preserve uncertainty where applicability cannot be established from available evidence.

universe_scope.temporal: Monitoring periods with monitoring_period_end_date (or equivalent) falling within 2024-10-01 through 2025-09-30 inclusive.
universe_scope.entities: Facilities, discharge/outfall features, parameters, limit sets/values, and DMR measurement events present in the compiled world for the three manifest facilities.
universe_scope.inclusion_rule: Evaluate only measurement/limit pairs where a reported measurement exists in source evidence; do not invent measurements.
universe_scope.exclusion_rule: Do not evaluate hypothetical unreported periods under Purpose A; those belong to Purposes B and C.

top_level.rows: list of evaluated measurement/limit pair objects
top_level.unresolved: list of cases whose applicability cannot be established

row_expectations: identify facility, discharge point/feature, parameter, and monitoring period
identify the applicable limit candidate or state that no enforceable numeric limit applies
state limit category: enforceable_numeric | report_only | no_numeric_comparison
when enforceable numeric limit is established and measurement is numeric, state comparison outcome: within_limit | exceeds_limit | comparison_not_applicable
grounding references to world relations and source evidence
unresolved_entry_expectations: state why applicability or comparison cannot be established

world_level: limit record exists in permit/limit extract
measurement record exists in DMR extract
limit has numeric value and unit
limit type/category flags from source (e.g., enforceable vs optional monitoring)
measurement has numeric reported value vs qualifier-only vs NODI
temporal overlap between limit effective dates and monitoring period
correspondence among facility, outfall, parameter, limit set, and DMR event
purpose_level: enforceable numeric limit applicable to this measurement context
monitoring present but no numeric compliance comparison applicable
measurement exceeds applicable enforceable numeric limit
measurement within applicable enforceable numeric limit

epistemic_requirements.grounding: Every persistent row verdict must cite grounded world assertions and source origins; no closed-world negation.
epistemic_requirements.uncertainty: When multiple limits could apply or unit/statistical-base alignment is ambiguous, do not silently pick; move to unresolved or state competing candidates explicitly.
epistemic_requirements.no_hidden_oracle: Applicability judgments are semantic-frontier work (C2/C3), not lookups against hidden expected outputs.
epistemic_requirements.separate_layers: World compiles what limits and measurements say; Purpose A applies policy to decide enforceability, applicability, and exceedance.

completeness_expectations.rows: One row per evaluated reported measurement in scope, or explicit unresolved entry when applicability cannot be established.
completeness_expectations.coverage: All FY2025 reported measurements for manifest facilities that enter the measurement/limit evaluation pipeline must appear in rows or unresolved.
completeness_expectations.receipt: Purpose output should be derivable from world relations plus purpose policies; downstream must not reread heterogeneous source files.

purpose_specific_policies.enforceability_threshold: Treat a limit as enforceable numeric only when purpose policy, grounded in permit/limit evidence, supports numeric compliance comparison for that measurement context.
purpose_specific_policies.report_only_classification: Classify as report_only when monitoring is required or reported but purpose policy finds no numeric exceedance comparison applies.
purpose_specific_policies.exceedance_rule: exceeds_limit is a purpose verdict requiring an established enforceable numeric limit, comparable numeric measurement, and policy-aligned unit/statistical comparison.
purpose_specific_policies.missing_data_rule: Absence of a numeric measurement does not by itself produce an exceedance or compliance verdict under Purpose A; route non-numeric/missing cases to Purpose C where appropriate.
purpose_specific_policies.policy_not_world: Labels enforceable_numeric, report_only, exceeds_limit, and within_limit are purpose classifications, not world primitives.

B.objective: For Federal FY2025, determine which monitoring requirements were actually applicable for the selected facilities, including requirements that depend on discharge occurrence, season, permit year, special studies, event conditions, or other permit conditions; for each evaluated requirement, determine whether evidence establishes monitoring was required, establishes it was not required, or leaves applicability unresolved.

universe_scope.temporal: Federal FY2025 and any permit-year or seasonal conditions that govern obligations during that window.
universe_scope.entities: Monitoring requirements derivable from permit limits, schedules, conditions, and facility context for NM0020583, NM0028762, NM0000116.
universe_scope.inclusion_rule: Evaluate monitoring requirements that the compiled evidence plausibly imposes or references for the period, including conditionally triggered requirements.
universe_scope.exclusion_rule: Do not treat Purpose B as numeric limit exceedance analysis (Purpose A) or as classification of missing numeric results (Purpose C).

top_level.rows: list of evaluated monitoring requirements and their applicability
top_level.unresolved: list of requirements whose applicability cannot be established

row_expectations: identify facility and monitoring requirement (parameter, outfall, frequency, condition trigger as relevant)
state applicability verdict: required | not_required | unresolved
when conditional, identify the condition basis (discharge occurrence, season, permit year, special study, event, other permit condition)
grounding references to world relations and source evidence
unresolved_entry_expectations: state which condition or evidence gap blocks resolution

world_level: monitoring requirement text/schedule exists in permit or limit extract
seasonal month flags or permit-year boundaries
discharge occurrence or no-discharge documentation in evidence
special study or event-driven requirement references
purpose_level: monitoring required for the evaluated period/context
monitoring not required for the evaluated period/context
conditional requirement whose trigger is satisfied
conditional requirement whose trigger is not satisfied

epistemic_requirements.grounding: Each required/not_required verdict must be grounded in explicit evidence; unresolved when triggers or scope cannot be established.
epistemic_requirements.conditionality: Conditional requirements must be evaluated against world-grounded facts about discharge, season, permit year, events, and studies—not assumed defaults.
epistemic_requirements.no_hidden_oracle: Obligation applicability is C2/C3 semantic work, not tuple completion from a hidden answer key.
epistemic_requirements.separate_layers: World records what permits and submissions say; Purpose B applies interpretive policy to decide actual applicability.

completeness_expectations.rows: Each evaluated monitoring requirement in scope appears with a required/not_required verdict or in unresolved.
completeness_expectations.coverage: Requirements tied to manifest facilities and FY2025-relevant schedules/conditions should be systematically enumerated from compiled world relations.
completeness_expectations.receipt: Output must be derivable from world.sqlite via purpose policies without rereading raw sources.

purpose_specific_policies.three_valued_logic: Every evaluated requirement must land in required, not_required, or unresolved; no silent default to required or not_required.
purpose_specific_policies.conditional_evaluation_order: Establish world facts about triggers first; only then apply purpose verdict on whether monitoring was actually required.
purpose_specific_policies.not_required_standard: not_required requires grounded evidence that the requirement does not apply (e.g., trigger false, out-of-season, no discharge, waived/superseded)—not mere absence of a DMR row.
purpose_specific_policies.policy_not_world: Verdicts required and not_required are purpose answers about applicability under analytical policy, not raw permit tuple existence.

C.objective: For Federal FY2025 monitoring expectations without an ordinary numeric reported result, determine what the available evidence establishes; distinguish documented no-discharge periods, periods where conditional monitoring was not required, other documented no-data states, required monitoring that appears to lack adequate evidence, and cases that remain unresolved; do not treat missing data by itself as evidence of compliance or violation.

universe_scope.temporal: Federal FY2025 monitoring periods where an expectation exists but no ordinary numeric DMR result is present.
universe_scope.entities: Monitoring expectations (from limits, schedules, obligations) crossed with DMR rows showing NODI, qualifiers, blank values, or absent submissions for manifest facilities.
universe_scope.inclusion_rule: Cases where monitoring was expected or plausibly expected and the available result is not an ordinary numeric measurement suitable for Purpose A comparison.
universe_scope.exclusion_rule: Do not re-adjudicate numeric exceedance (Purpose A) or re-decide whether monitoring was required when that is the sole question (Purpose B), except where overlap requires consistent cross-reference.

top_level.rows: list of evaluated no-result / NODI / missing-evidence cases and the established state
top_level.unresolved: list of cases that remain unresolved

row_expectations: identify facility, monitoring expectation, and period
classify established state using the purpose taxonomy below
cite evidence for the classification (NODI code, permit no-discharge documentation, conditional relief, etc.)
do not infer compliance or violation from absence alone
unresolved_entry_expectations: state why evidence is inadequate to classify

world_level: DMR row exists with NODI code or non-numeric qualifier
no DMR row present for an expected period
permit or submission documents no discharge
conditional monitoring relief grounded in permit or operational evidence
documented no-data reason codes or narrative in source

epistemic_requirements.grounding: Classifications must be grounded in explicit evidence; missing rows alone are not sufficient for compliance or violation conclusions.
epistemic_requirements.conservative_inference: When evidence does not establish a documented no-data reason, prefer required_monitoring_lacks_adequate_evidence or unresolved over compliance/violation inference.
epistemic_requirements.no_hidden_oracle: Missing-evidence semantics are interpretive (C2/C3), not pattern-matching to hidden labels.
epistemic_requirements.separate_layers: World records submissions, NODI codes, and permit statements; Purpose C applies taxonomy policy to state what has been established.

completeness_expectations.rows: Each in-scope no-result / missing-evidence case receives a taxonomy classification or appears in unresolved.
completeness_expectations.coverage: FY2025 monitoring expectations without ordinary numeric results for manifest facilities should be enumerated from compiled relations.
completeness_expectations.cross_purpose_consistency: Classifications should remain consistent with Purpose B obligation verdicts and Purpose A's refusal to treat missing data as exceedance/compliance.

taxonomy.documented_no_discharge_period: Evidence explicitly establishes no discharge for the period.
taxonomy.conditional_monitoring_not_required: Evidence establishes a conditional monitoring obligation did not apply (aligned with Purpose B when available).
taxonomy.other_documented_no_data_state: Evidence establishes a specific no-data reason that is neither no-discharge nor conditional relief (e.g., documented NODI meaning).
taxonomy.required_monitoring_lacks_adequate_evide: Monitoring appears required but available evidence does not adequately document result or acceptable no-data basis.
taxonomy.unresolved: Evidence insufficient to select among the above.

purpose_specific_policies.non_inference_rule: Missing data, blank fields, or unexplained absence must not by itself be treated as compliance or violation.
purpose_specific_policies.policy_not_world: The five-way purpose taxonomy is an analytical classification scheme, not a world primitive; world stores observations and grounded judgments only.
